data.text:
I have enough evidence. Summary of findings:

- **WAN interface (vtnet0)** is UP with a valid lease (`198.51.100.27`) and a default route via `198.51.100.1`, but `arp -a` shows the next hop `198.51.100.1` as **(incomplete)** — no L2 resolution.
- `ping 198.51.100.1` fails with **`sendto: No buffer space available`** (ENOBUFS) — the transmit path on vtnet0 is wedged.
- `dmesg` shows repeated **`vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0`** with link DOWN/UP cycles — a virtio NIC TX queue hang.
- The WAN watchdog performed **4 reloads during this outage (all rc=0)** and hit its `reload_cap` (12/24h) at 03:30, yet connectivity never returned — so DHCP/reload succeeds but traffic can't flow through the stuck driver.
- The cable modem is now **OPERATIONAL** (after a T3-timeout reboot ~02:28), so the provider side recovered; the internet remains down because of the firewall's own hung WAN NIC.
- LAN is healthy (`ping 10.20.0.9` OK), local services fine.

A `wan_reload` reconfigures the interface/DHCP but does not reset the wedged vtnet0 driver (already proven by 4 ineffective reloads). A full firewall restart is needed to reinitialize the NIC.

data.reason: The firewall's WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit path has hung (repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0"), so packets cannot leave toward the ISP even though the interface is up and has a valid lease, leaving the internet down while LAN works.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit path has hung (repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0"), so packets cannot leave toward the ISP even though the interface is up and has a valid lease, leaving the internet down while LAN works.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' with link DOWN/UP cycles
arp -a -n shows next hop 198.51.100.1 as '(incomplete)' — no L2 resolution
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 fails with 'sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS), 100% loss
ifconfig vtnet0 shows status active with IP 198.51.100.27; netstat -rn shows default via 198.51.100.1
/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json: reloads_in_outage=4, last_action=reload, modem_op_since set; events.jsonl shows 4 reloads rc=0 during outage then 'reload_cap' reached at 03:30 with no recovery
modem-events/modem-metrics show modem rebooted ~02:28 and now OPERATIONAL, so provider side recovered
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (gw.lan) to reinitialize the hung vtnet0 WAN NIC; a wan_reload is insufficient because it does not reset the stuck virtio driver (4 reloads already had no effect). The maintainer is away, so let the harness decide/queue the reboot. Do not bother with modem_reboot — the modem is already OPERATIONAL.
